items.title: Analyzer projections of a two-dimensional polarisation space and their overlaps
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
the spectral values $1$ and $0$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator
$P_{\theta}$ have projections $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$,
respectively. These two alternatives may be labelled $+1$ and $-1$ in a
declared analyser; those labels are not the spectral values of $P_{\theta}$.
The eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

items.title: Restricted momentum and energy multipliers of the transverse one-photon space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited multiplication and spectral items. On
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]])
put
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f:\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\},$$
a closed subspace of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$, and write
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$, $\Pi(0):=0$, so that
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}$ with $M_{\Pi}$ the bounded
multiplication by $\Pi$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]). Let
$c,\hbar>0$ with $c$ in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and $\hbar$ in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$, and for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $m\in\{\hbar k_{j},\ \hbar c|k|\}$
define
$$D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}):=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\ \textstyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}m(k)^{2}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k<\infty\},\qquad M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f:=mf .$$
Then for each such $m$:

(a) $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on the
Hilbert space $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and it is the
restriction to $\mathfrak h$ of the self-adjoint multiplier $M_{m}$ on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]];

(b) its spectral projection-valued measure $E_{m}$ is given by
$$E_{m}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}\bigr|_{\mathfrak h}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
and for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$ the outcome law $B\mapsto\|E_{m}(B)f\|^{2}$
is the push-forward of the finite measure $|f|^{2}\,d^{3}k\big|_{\mathfrak h}$
under $k\mapsto m(k)$; in particular for $m=\hbar k_{j}$ it is the push-forward
under $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$ and for $m=\hbar c|k|$ it is the push-forward under
$k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]);

(c) $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues: for no $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is
there a nonzero $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ with $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f=\lambda f$;

(d) for every unit $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ one has
$$\operatorname{Var}_{f}(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}):=\|M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f\|^{2}-\langle M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle^{2}>0;$$
consequently no unit vector of $\mathfrak h$ has a sharp $m$-value.

The identifications of $\mathfrak h$ and of these multipliers with physical
transverse photons, momenta or energies are not asserted here; they are a
separate model assignment outside this lemma.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.4 printed pages 73-74 (PDF pages 85-86): multiplication operators, their spectra and the absence of eigenvalues on null level sets

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Chapter 1 Section 1.4 printed pages 7-9 (PDF pages 10-12): second-quantised single-particle operators and the energy of free modes

items.title: The fixed-mode isometry of Fock space and the transfer of number and ladder operators
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). By
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], Choice supplies the
Dependent Choice hypothesis, as defined in [[def-dependent-choice]], of the
cited transverse free-field Fock result.
Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$, sector
projections $\Pi_n$, number operator $N$ and maximal creation and annihilation
operators $A_\pm(f)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] and
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a unit
vector $\varphi\in H$. Write $\varphi^{\otimes0}:=1\in\mathbb C$ and
$\varphi^{\otimes n}:=\varphi\otimes\cdots\otimes\varphi\in H^{\otimes n}$ for
$n\ge1$, and define
$$U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H),\qquad U_\varphi e_n:=(0,\dots,0,\varphi^{\otimes n},0,\dots)$$
with the entry in coordinate $n$, extended linearly. Then:

(a) each $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$; the family $(\varphi^{\otimes n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$
is orthonormal in $F(H)$, and $U_\varphi$ is a linear isometry of
$F(\mathbb C)$ onto the closed subspace
$\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\varphi^{\otimes n}:n\in\mathbb N\}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(b) for every $\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\in F(\mathbb C)$ and every $n$,
$$\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi,\qquad \|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2},$$
where $\Pi_n'$ is the Fock sector projection of $F(\mathbb C)$; and for every
$\psi\in D(N')$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ with
$$NU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi N'\psi ;$$

(c) for every $\psi\in D(A_\pm(1))$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_\pm(\varphi))$
and
$$A_\pm(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_\pm(1)\psi ;$$
in particular for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the coherent vector
$\psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] satisfies
$U_\varphi\psi_z\in D(A_-(\varphi))$ and $A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi_z=z\,U_\varphi\psi_z$;

(d) for the transverse case $H=\mathfrak h$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$, and a unit
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h\cap D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ (so that
$\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$), one has
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi e_n,U_\varphi e_n\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
and for every $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$ with $\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}<\infty$
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi\psi,U_\varphi\psi\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n|\psi_n|^{2}\Bigr)\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle N'\psi,\psi\rangle\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle ;$$
Already under $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing $\bar\varepsilon=\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle$, the finite spectral second moment is
$$\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\|\varepsilon\varphi\|^2+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^2.$$
If moreover $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2})$, the vector lies in $D(T_n^2)$ and this norm square equals the literal operator pairing below; then
$$\langle T_n\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle T_n^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle+n(n-1)\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle^{2}.$$

No physical interpretation of the isometry, of the vectors
$U_\varphi e_n$, or of the transferred operators is asserted.

items.title: Total momentum multipliers on transverse symmetric Fock sectors
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), carrying the actual hypotheses of the multiplier and Fock suppliers. Fix a positive real parameter $\hbar$ and let
$$G=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \mathfrak h=\{f\in G:k\cdot f(k)=0\text{ for a.e. }k\},\qquad \Pi(k)=I-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}\ (k\ne0),\quad \Pi(0)=0.$$
Use the Hilbert tensor powers of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], the symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], and the Fock space of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], with sectors $\mathfrak H_n=\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\subset\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}$ for $n\ge1$ and $\mathfrak H_0=\mathbb C$.

For $n\ge1$ there is a canonical isometric embedding
$$I_n:\mathfrak H_n\longrightarrow L_n:=L^2(\mathbb R^{3n};(\mathbb C^3)^{\otimes n}),$$
obtained by inclusion into $G^{\otimes n}$ followed by the iterated finite-component Euclidean product unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. On elementary tensors before symmetrization that unitary sends $f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n$ to $(k_1,\ldots,k_n)\mapsto f_1(k_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n(k_n)$. Write $K_n=I_n\mathfrak H_n$, a closed subspace. For $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ put
$$p_{j,n}(k_1,\ldots,k_n)=\hbar\sum_{i=1}^n(k_i)_j,\qquad D(P_{j,n})=\{u\in\mathfrak H_n:p_{j,n}I_nu\in L_n\},\qquad P_{j,n}u=I_n^{-1}(p_{j,n}I_nu).$$
The displayed product always lies in $K_n$ whenever it lies in $L_n$, so this action is well-defined. Set $P_{j,0}=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Then:

**(a) Sector self-adjointness and spectral measure.** Every $P_{j,n}$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on its sector. For Borel $B\subset\mathbb R$, its regular spectral PVM is
$$E_{j,n}(B)u=I_n^{-1}(\mathbf1_{p_{j,n}^{-1}(B)}I_nu)\quad(n\ge1),\qquad E_{j,0}(B)=\mathbf1_B(0)I_{\mathbb C}.$$
In particular $D(P_{j,n})$ is exactly the square-integrability domain of the signed summed multiplier, without requiring the individual summands to be square integrable separately.

**(b) Total momentum.** On $F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_n$ define
$$D(P_j)=\{\psi:\psi_n\in D(P_{j,n})\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_{n\ge0}\|P_{j,n}\psi_n\|^2<\infty\},\qquad (P_j\psi)_n=P_{j,n}\psi_n.$$
Then $P_j$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on precisely this domain. Equivalently its domain is given by
$$\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{\mathbb R^{3n}}|p_{j,n}(k)|^2\|I_n\psi_n(k)\|^2\,d^{3n}k<\infty.$$
Its regular spectral PVM is the sectorwise direct sum
$$E_j(B)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}E_{j,n}(B),\qquad P_j=\int_{\mathbb R}t\,dE_j(t).$$
For every $\psi\in F(\mathfrak h)$, without a domain assumption, its scalar spectral measure is
$$\langle E_j(B)\psi,\psi\rangle=\mathbf1_B(0)|\psi_0|^2+\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{p_{j,n}^{-1}(B)}\|I_n\psi_n(k)\|^2\,d^{3n}k.$$
Thus it is the sum of the sectorwise push-forward measures and the vacuum atom. The vacuum belongs to $D(P_j)$ and $P_j\Omega=0$. On the one-particle sector the operator is the restricted multiplier $f\mapsto\hbar k_jf$ on its maximal square-integrability domain.

These are mathematical operator/domain statements. They adopt no photon assignment, probability law, dispersion relation, dynamical law or relation between momentum, energy and number operators.

items.title: Radiation extension of the framework: transverse mode and photon assignments
items.statement:
Adopt, as an additional model assumption of the framework on this page and its
consumers, the following radiation extension. It is adopted together with the
state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), in the space vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the species and
sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and the units and dimensions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). By
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], the stated Axiom of
Choice entails Dependent Choice, as defined in [[def-dependent-choice]],
supplying the DC hypothesis of the cited
transverse free-field Fock theorem without adopting an additional choice axiom.

**(i) Fixed propagation-mode one-photon polarisation model.** For a declared
propagation mode, described by a nonzero wavevector label
$k_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ read in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in a declared
inertial chart ([[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]]), the model assigns a
two-dimensional complex internal space, the **transverse polarisation space**
of the mode: the complex span of an orthonormal pair $(v_{1},v_{2})$ of vectors
of $\mathbb C^{3}$ satisfying $k_{0}\cdot v_{1}=k_{0}\cdot v_{2}=0$, with the
standard Hermitian form. Unit rays of this space are the model's **one-photon
polarisation preparations** of the mode. This assignment is an idealised
manifestation of the abstract Born/state framework on a finite-dimensional
internal factor; it is not a spatial wave function of a massive particle, not a
model of a photon position, and not the massive one-particle Hamiltonian of P5
with mass set to zero. For the massive free family,
[[cex-nrqm-framework-zero-mass-has-no-self-adjoint-limit]] refutes strong
action convergence to a self-adjoint operator on every Schwartz state and
shows frequency divergence at each fixed nonzero wave number as
$m\downarrow0$. This extension uses its independently declared massless
model assignments, with no such limiting construction.

**(ii) Quantised transverse radiation sector.** The model assigns to the free
radiation a **bosonic species** in the sense of P6, whose one-particle space is
the transverse space
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^{2}$ inner product; its $n$-particle sector is
$\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}=\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$ and its radiation state
space is the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
  [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]). The
  choice of a bosonic species is the additional model assignment of P6 clause
  (iii). It is adopted here, not derived from the preceding assumptions, and
  this item records no experimental observation that establishes it.

**(iii) Mode assignments of frequency, energy and momentum.** In the declared
inertial chart, each free mode label $k\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ is
assigned the **angular frequency** $\omega(k):=c|k|$ in $\mathrm s^{-1}$, the
**photon energy** $E(k):=\hbar\omega(k)=\hbar c|k|$ in joules and the
**photon momentum** $p(k):=\hbar k$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
where $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}\ \mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and
$\hbar=h/(2\pi)>0$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$ have the SI values of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (c). Ordinary frequency is
$\nu(k)=\omega(k)/(2\pi)$ in hertz. These are separate quantum-radiation model
assignments: they are neither consequences of classical Maxwell theory nor
consequences of the special-relativistic framework, and no Lorentz
transformation law for the mode label $k$, for $\omega(k)$ or for the
polarisation pair is adopted or claimed; the extension does not assert Galilean
covariance of the radiation sector, and it does not identify the massless
Lorentz representations of the photon with the representations of the spatial
rotation group used in P6.

Littlejohn's Section 7 derives the normal-ordered free-field momentum from the
field momentum density and obtains
$P=\sum_{\lambda}\hbar k\,a_{\lambda}^{\dagger}a_{\lambda}$, then reads an
occupation-number state as carrying the corresponding sum of photon momenta
(equations (21)-(33)). That derivation uses Gaussian units, Coulomb gauge and box
normalization; it supports this assignment but does not derive this framework's
other radiation assumptions or its covariance claims.

**(iv) Free-field observables.** The model assigns the total free-field energy
observable $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ and
$T_{n}\psi=\varepsilon_{n}\psi$, read in joules, the total number observable $N$
read in the dimensionless unit $1$ of counted quanta, and the total momentum
components $\bigoplus_n\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\hbar k_{j,i}\bigr)$, read in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; their operator domains and
self-adjointness are the mathematics of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] for energy and
number, and [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-fock-total-momentum]] for total
momentum, read physically in
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]].
The total momentum components use the maximal signed summed-multiplier
sector domains and the squared-norm summability Fock domain of that lemma;
the vacuum has total momentum zero.

**(v) Counting, detection and light-matter coupling are not supplied.** Photon
number and energy *statistics* require a declared detector model in the sense
of P2 and P7, which this postulate does not supply; a prescribed classical
electromagnetic field does not by itself yield photon counting or vacuum
spontaneous emission. No light-matter Hamiltonian, no dipole coupling, no
emission or absorption process and no recoil model is asserted here; the
absorption/stimulated-emission branch with a finite-level dipole coupling and
the quantised-mode emission construction are separate model assumptions for
the later pair on light-matter and spectral transitions. The relation of a
laboratory field, polariser or detector to this model is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of the postulate.

**(vi) Scope of the framework.** The radiation extension is deliberately
non-relativistic in its matter sector: it adds external free radiation modes to
the fixed-particle-number massive matter core without changing P5. Relativistic
matter, antiparticles, pair creation, covariant local field dynamics and full
quantum electrodynamics are not contained in this extension and are not
disguised as solved core prerequisites; they require a named field-theory
destination. No position wave function of the photon satisfying the massive
Schrödinger equation is introduced.

**(vii) Status.** Clauses (i)-(vi) are adopted assumptions of the model. They
are motivated by the sources cited above -- the transverse two-state
description of polarisation with transmitted fraction $\cos^{2}\theta$, the
single-mode oscillator quantisation with photon energy increment $\hbar\omega$,
and the field-operator expansion of free modes -- but motivation is not
deduction. No empirical claim, no measured value and no claim that any
laboratory field, polariser or detector is exactly described by the model is
made by this item.
items.physical_scope: The adopted radiation extension of the non-relativistic quantum framework: a fixed propagation-mode one-photon polarisation model with a two-dimensional transverse internal space, and a quantised free transverse radiation sector with bosonic Fock space and the mode assignments omega=c|k|, photon energy E=hbar*omega and photon momentum p=hbar*k in a declared inertial laboratory chart. The extension is an explicitly adopted model assumption; it is not derived from classical Maxwell theory, from special relativity, or from the massive-particle model by a mass-to-zero limit, and no Lorentz transformation law for the mode labels and no Galilean covariance of the radiation sector are claimed. Detection, coupling to matter and spontaneous emission are not supplied by this postulate.

items.title: The radiation sector of the framework: modes and the number, energy and momentum assignments
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 and the identical-particle and spin
postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) and the radiation
extension postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] in
its clauses (i)-(iv), read in the state vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the sector
vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
Fock space mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Radiation one-particle space and sectors.** The **transverse one-particle
space** of the radiation sector is
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\}$$
with the restricted $L^{2}$ inner product, a separable complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]); its elements are read as **one-photon wave-packet
vectors**. The wave-vector coordinate is $k$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and the
normalization is against $d^{3}k$. With normalized state vectors dimensionless,
a unit wave-packet vector $f$ therefore has coordinate representatives $f(k)$
with units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$, so that $\int\|f(k)\|^{2}d^{3}k$ is
dimensionless. A unit mode vector has the same coordinate units. For $n\ge1$
the **$n$-photon sector** is
$\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}=\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}\subseteq\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}$
and the **radiation state space** is the bosonic Fock space
$F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, whose sector projections
are $\Pi_n$ and whose vacuum is $\Omega=\iota_0(1)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]]). A **declared
radiation preparation** is a state $\rho\in D(F(\mathfrak h))$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]; a **declared one-photon
preparation** is a preparation whose state is supported in the one-photon
sector, and for a unit $f\in\mathfrak h$ the ray of $\iota_{1}(f)$ is the
one-photon preparation **of wave-packet vector $f$**.

**(c) Modes.** A **mode** of the radiation sector is a ray
$[\varphi]=\{z\varphi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a nonzero class
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, equivalently the rank-one orthogonal projection onto
$\mathbb C\varphi$. Its unit representatives differ only by a complex factor
of modulus one. A **declared mode family** is a
finite or countable orthonormal family $(\varphi_{j})$ of $\mathfrak h$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For
a unit mode vector $\varphi$ and a dimensionless label $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector
$$U_\varphi\psi_z,\qquad \psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n,$$
is the **mode-coherent preparation vector of label $z$**, and $U_\varphi e_n$
is the **$n$-quanta mode vector**; these are the readings of the transferred
vectors of [[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. A mode vector is a
normalisable wave packet; the sharp-mode label $k$ of the propagation-mode
idealisation is a spectral parameter and is not a state of $\mathfrak h$
([[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]
clause (c)).

**(d) Assigned observables.** The framework assigns to the radiation sector:

1. the **total number observable** $(N,1)$, the self-adjoint number operator of
   [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], with domain
   $D(N)=\{\psi:\sum_nn^{2}\|\psi_n\|^{2}<\infty\}$ and read in the
   dimensionless unit $1$ of counted quanta;
2. the **free-field energy observable** $(H_f,\mathrm J)$, the operator
   $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ and
   $T_{n}\psi=\varepsilon_{n}\psi$, of
   [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
   read in joules; its one-particle restriction is the energy multiplier
   $M_{\hbar c|k|}^{\mathfrak h}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]];
3. for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ the **total momentum component** $(P_j,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ is the self-adjoint direct sum of the signed summed multipliers $P_{j,n}$ of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-fock-total-momentum]], with $P_{j,0}=0$. In the lemma's exact Euclidean embedding $I_n$ of each symmetric transverse sector, $P_{j,n}$ multiplies by $p_{j,n}(k)=\hbar\sum_i(k_i)_j$ on the maximal domain $\{u:p_{j,n}I_nu\in L^2\}$. Its Fock domain is
   $$D(P_j)=\{\psi:\psi_n\in D(P_{j,n})\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_n\|P_{j,n}\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}.$$
   This is the domain of the sum, without an extra requirement that each individual momentum summand be square integrable. Its spectral PVM is the sectorwise direct sum of the inverse-image indicator multipliers, including the atom at zero on the vacuum. The **one-photon momentum component** is its restriction to sector one, identified with $M_{\hbar k_j}^{\mathfrak h}$ of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]. The postulate assigns these mathematical operators their physical momentum meaning and units.

**(e) Reading of the mode assignments.** In the declared inertial chart the
assignments $\omega(k)=c|k|$ in $\mathrm s^{-1}$, $E(k)=\hbar\omega(k)$ in
$\mathrm J$ and $p(k)=\hbar k$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ of
clause (iii) of the radiation postulate are read through the spectral measures
of clause (d): for a one-photon preparation of unit wave-packet vector
$f\in\mathfrak h$, the **assigned frequency**, **energy** and
**momentum component** laws are the push-forwards of the measure
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto c|k|$,
$k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$ and $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$; these laws, and their finite means under the corresponding first-moment conditions, are proved on this page. Sharp
frequency, sharp energy and sharp momentum-component states are not vectors of
$\mathfrak h$; every unit one-photon vector in the corresponding multiplier domain has
finite strictly positive variance in that quantity (clause (d) of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]).
The push-forward laws themselves exist for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$, without a moment-domain assumption; all their singleton probabilities vanish by the null level sets in the cited lemma, so they are non-Dirac laws even when finite means or variances do not exist. Thus "photon of energy $\hbar\omega$" names a spectral assignment of the model, not a normalisable state with an exact energy.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) fix the sector assignment and the units. They
assert no detector model, no sampling model, no dynamics, no interaction with
matter, no spontaneous emission and no empirical result; the counting and detection vocabulary is fixed separately on this page. The
identification of a laboratory radiation field with a preparation of
$F(\mathfrak h)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7, and no
Lorentz transformation law for modes or their labels is adopted or claimed.
items.physical_scope: The reading of the radiation extension postulate in the framework's vocabulary: the transverse one-particle space, the bosonic Fock sector assignment, the vocabulary of modes and mode families, normalized one-photon wave-packet coordinates f(k) in m^(3/2) under d^3k and dimensionless coherent-state labels z, the assigned total-number observable in the dimensionless unit 1, the assigned free-field energy observable in joules with epsilon(k)=hbar*c*|k|, and the assigned total momentum components and their one-photon restrictions in kg m s^-1 with the mode assignments omega=c|k|, E=hbar*omega and p=hbar*k. The readings record operator domains and self-adjointness from the cited mathematics; they assert no detector response, no light-matter coupling, no dynamics, no Lorentz transformation law and no empirical result.

items.title: The fixed-mode polarisation model of the framework
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement
postulate P3, the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and the radiation
extension postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] in
its clause (i). Read the state vocabulary in
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable vocabulary
in [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
measurement vocabulary in
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], and
the units of angles in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: angles and
phases are dimensionless under the radian convention. Assume Countable Choice,
Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), including the hypotheses inherited from the adopted
radiation postulate and its Fock-space suppliers.

**(b) Declared fixed-mode data.** A **declared fixed-mode polarisation model**
consists of:

1. a nonzero **propagation label** $k_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$, read
   in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in a declared inertial chart, which is a parameter of the
   model and not a state;
2. a declared **transverse frame**, that is a pair $v_j=\zeta u_j$ for
   $j\in\{1,2\}$, where $(u_1,u_2)$ is a real orthonormal basis of
   $k_0^\perp:=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:k_0\cdot u=0\}$ and $\zeta\in\mathbb C$
   is one common phase factor, $|\zeta|=1$. Here $k_0\cdot u$ is the real
   Euclidean dot product, and the Hermitian form on $\mathbb C^3$ is
   $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_{\ell=1}^3 x_\ell\overline{y_\ell}$, linear
   in its first argument; thus $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}$ and
   $k_0\cdot v_j:=\sum_{\ell=1}^3(k_0)_\ell(v_j)_\ell=0$;
3. the **polarisation space** $V:=\mathbb Cv_{1}\oplus\mathbb Cv_{2}$ with the
   restricted Hermitian inner product and the orthonormal basis
   $(e_{1},e_{2}):=(v_{1},v_{2})$.

The model's **state space** is $D(V)$, the set of density operators of $V$; the
**pure preparations** of the model are the unit rays $[\psi]$ of $V$, that is
the preparations assigned the pure state $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], and a **mixed
preparation** is a statistical mixture of preparations in the sense of P1.
A pure ray is **linearly polarised** when it has a nonzero real representative
in $k_0^\perp$. The map
$\theta\mapsto\psi_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2}$ assigns
to each angle $\theta\in\mathbb R$ a distinguished pure preparation, the
**linear polarisation preparation at angle $\theta$** in the declared
transverse frame. In particular,
$\psi_\theta=\zeta(\cos\theta\,u_1+\sin\theta\,u_2)$ has that ray, whose
real direction is the unoriented line
$\mathbb R(\cos\theta\,u_1+\sin\theta\,u_2)$; hence the physical angle
label is modulo $\pi$. General complex unit vectors of $V$ remain allowed as
pure preparations and need not be linearly polarised.

**(c) Declared polarisation analyser.** For each angle $\theta\in\mathbb R$ the
**declared polarisation analyser at angle $\theta$** is the declared ideal
sharp measurement of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] with
two outcomes labelled $+1$ and $-1$ and outcome structure
$$(P_{\theta},\,P_{\theta}^{\perp}),\qquad P_{\theta}x=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta},\quad e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}:=I-P_{\theta},$$
whose projections $P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are those of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]]. The **outcome law** of
the analyser in a preparation $\rho$ is the reading of P2 for the projections
of the outcome structure, and the labels are dimensionless with the reading
"$+1$: transmitted", "$-1$: blocked". Where a conditional post-measurement
state is used, it is the Lueders update of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]; the
framework does not assert that a laboratory absorber leaves an outgoing
one-photon polarisation state, and the absorption outcome is used only through
its discarded-outcome law unless a separate instrument is declared (clause (v)
of P3).

**(d) Frame covariance and angle labels.** For another complex orthonormal transverse pair $(e_1',e_2')$ (not necessarily a transverse frame of clause (b)), let $U:V\to V$ be the unitary map with $Ue_i=e_i'$, explicitly $Ux=\sum_i\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i'$. Its transported sharp-measurement family is $P_\theta'=UP_\theta U^*$, because $Ue_\theta=\cos\theta e_1'+\sin\theta e_2'$. Under the simultaneous transport of a preparation to $\rho'=U\rho U^*$ the Born probabilities agree: $\operatorname{tr}(\rho'P_\theta')=\operatorname{tr}(U\rho P_\theta U^*)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\theta)$. The last equality follows by evaluating the finite trace in a transported orthonormal basis; the same argument preserves trace one, and conjugation preserves positivity and self-adjointness of $\rho$. Thus covariance concerns the transported states and projectors together. A general complex basis change need not leave the original linear-analyser family fixed: replacing $e_2$ by $ie_2$ gives rays of $\cos\theta e_1+i\sin\theta e_2$, generally absent from the original family, and does not satisfy clause (b). For two transverse frames of clause (b), the bases differ by a common phase times a real orthogonal two-by-two matrix. Write its first column as $(\cos\chi,\sin\chi)$; its second column is $(-\sin\chi,\cos\chi)$ or $(\sin\chi,-\cos\chi)$ according to whether its determinant is $+1$ or $-1$. The families are equal with the angle reparametrisation $\theta\mapsto\chi+\theta$ or $\chi-\theta$, respectively, by the sine and cosine addition formulas. Arbitrary complex basis transport gives a valid sharp measurement but need not give a linear polariser. The value of $|k_0|$ enters no polarisation probability: it enters the separate mode frequency and energy assignments of the radiation postulate.

**(e) Scope.** The model is an idealisation of a transverse propagation mode
with a definite mode label. It is a finite-dimensional internal-factor model
in the sense of P1 and P6: its state space is $D(V)$, its pure preparations are
rays, and its analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement. It contains no
position observable, no momentum observable, no spatial wave function and no
localisation claim, and it is not the massive one-particle model of P5 with
$m=0$ and is not obtained from that model by a mass-to-zero limit; no such
limit is used or claimed. The mode label $k_{0}$ is not a
normalisable state of any sector of the framework, and a plane wave is not
introduced as a state. Whether a laboratory polariser and source realize this
declared model, with what efficiency, loss and background, is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of this
definition.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model data, its outcome vocabulary and
its scope; they add no assumption beyond the cited postulates and the cited
finite-dimensional mathematics. The mathematical properties of the projections
are the content of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]]; the conditional outcome law of the declared analyser is proved on this page. No empirical claim is made here.
items.physical_scope: The declared fixed propagation-mode polarisation model of the framework: a nonzero wavevector label, a declared real orthonormal pair spanning the real transverse plane with an optional common phase, the two-dimensional complex polarisation space with its unit rays as idealised one-photon polarisation preparations, and the two-outcome polarisation analyser family with the Born outcome law of P2 and the Lueders reading of P3 where used. The model is an adopted idealisation of a transverse mode with a definite propagation label; it is not a spatial wave function, has no position or momentum observable, is not the massless limit of the massive model, and asserts no localisation, no detector response, no loss, no efficiency and no empirical result.

items.title: The analyser outcome law of the fixed-mode polarisation model: Born probabilities and the Malus ratio
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), the radiation
extension postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], in the state
vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
observable and measurement vocabularies of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]].
Assume Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]),
including the hypotheses inherited from the radiation postulate and the cited
spectral and measurement mathematics. Fix angles
$\varphi,\theta,\theta'\in\mathbb R$ and write
$\psi_{\varphi}=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ and
$P_{\theta}$ for the analyser projections of the model. Then:

(a) the declared polarisation analyser at angle $\theta$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement with outcome structure $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$, the
outcome labels $+1$ and $-1$ naming the first and second projection, in
the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]:
$P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are bounded orthogonal projections with
$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$ and $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$;

(b) the spectral projection-valued measure $E$ of the bounded self-adjoint
operator $P_{\theta}$ (assigned with unit $1$; its values on the two outcomes
are $1$ and $0$, while the analyser labels are $+1$ and $-1$) satisfies
$$E(\{1\})=P_{\theta},\qquad E(\{0\})=P_{\theta}^{\perp},\qquad E(\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\})=0,$$
consequently the outcome law of the assigned sharp quantity $P_{\theta}$ in a
preparation $\rho\in D(V)$ is
$$p_{+1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}),\qquad p_{-1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp})=1-p_{+1}(\rho),$$
which is exactly the law of the declared analyser;

(c) for the linear-polarisation preparation $\psi_{\varphi}$ and a general
pure preparation with unit vector $\psi=\alpha e_{1}+\beta e_{2}$,
$$p_{+1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{-1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{+1}(\psi)=|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta|^{2};$$
for a statistical mixture $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ of preparations the law
is affine, $p_{+1}(\rho)=\sum_{n}w_{n}p_{+1}(\rho_{n})$;

(d) the law is invariant under the phase of the preparation and under the
phase of the analysed direction: $p_{+1}$ depends only on the rays
$[\psi_{\varphi}]$ and $[e_{\theta}]$, is $2\pi$-periodic in each argument, and
satisfies $p_{+1}(\theta,\varphi)=p_{+1}(\theta-\varphi,0)$;

(e) if $p_{+1}(\rho)>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $+1$ of the
analyser is $\rho_{+1}=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}/p_{+1}(\rho)$; for the pure
preparation $[\psi_{\varphi}]$ with $\cos(\theta-\varphi)\ne0$ it is the pure
state of the analysed ray $[e_{\theta}]$, and a second analyser at angle
$\theta'$ then gives the conditional probability
$\cos^{2}(\theta'-\theta)$ for the outcome $+1$. If the outcome is discarded,
the state is $\Phi(\rho)=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp}$;

(f) the assertions (a)-(e) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P3 and the
adopted model. They assert no dynamics, no laboratory polariser, no detector
efficiency, no loss, no sampling model and no empirical result; in particular
the fraction $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ is a model probability of the declared
ideal analyser, not a measured count.
items.physical_scope: The conditional outcome law of the declared polarisation analyser of the fixed propagation-mode model: the analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement with projections P_theta and P_theta-perp, its Born law in a pure linear-polarisation preparation is cos^2(theta-phi) and sin^2(theta-phi), the law is affine over statistical mixtures and invariant under the phases of the preparation, the conditional post-passage state is the analysed polarisation ray, and a second ideal analyser gives the relative cos^2 law. The result is conditional on P1, P2, P3 and the adopted model; no laboratory polariser is identified with the declared ideal analyser and no empirical result is asserted.

items.title: Number, energy and momentum laws of a one-photon preparation
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], in
the state vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
the observable vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Assume Countable
Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), including the hypotheses
inherited from the radiation postulate and the cited operator and spectral
items.
Let $f\in\mathfrak h$ be a unit one-photon wave-packet vector. Under the
$d^{3}k$ normalization of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], its
coordinate representatives $f(k)$ have units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$. Put
$\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, and let
$\rho_{f}$ be the one-photon preparation of the ray of $\iota_{1}(f)$. Then:

(a) *number law*: the outcome law of the assigned total-number observable
$(N,1)$ in $\rho_{f}$ is $\mu^{N}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\mathbf 1_{B}(1)$ for every
Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$: the number readout of the one-photon
preparation is one with probability one;

(b) *frequency and energy laws*: the assigned frequency law
$\mu^{\omega}_{\rho_f}$ and the outcome law of the assigned free-field energy observable
$(H_f,\mathrm J)$ in $\rho_{f}$ are the push-forwards of
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto c|k|$ and
$k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$, respectively:
$$\mu^{\omega}_{\rho_f}(B)=\int_{\{k:c|k|\in B\}}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad \mu^{H_f}_{\rho_f}(B)=\int_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
and if $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|k|\,\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k<\infty$, their spectral-law means are
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\omega\,d\mu^{\omega}_{\rho_f}(\omega)=c\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|k|\,\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}E\,d\mu^{H_f}_{\rho_f}(E)=\hbar c\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|k|\,\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k;$$

(c) *momentum readouts*: for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ the one-photon momentum-component
readout of clause (d)(3) of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] has,
in the identification of the one-photon sector with $\mathfrak h$ by
$\iota_{1}$, the outcome law
$$\mu^{P_{j}}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\int_{\{k:\hbar k_{j}\in B\}}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the push-forward of $\|f\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$, with mean
$\hbar\int k_{j}\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ whenever
$\int |k_{j}|\,\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k<\infty$;

(d) *no sharp frequency, energy or momentum*: for every unit vector
$f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, the variances of the frequency and energy
laws of (b) are strictly positive, and for every unit vector in
$D(M_{\hbar k_j}^{\mathfrak h})$ the momentum-component variance of (c) is
strictly positive; consequently the mode assignment "photon energy $E=\hbar\omega$,
$\omega=c|k|$" is a spectral assignment of the model and never an exact value
of a normalisable one-photon state;

(e) all assertions are conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model;
they record no detector model, no sampling model, no measured count and no
empirical claim.
items.physical_scope: The outcome laws of the assigned radiation observables in a declared one-photon preparation of the model: the number observable has the sharp value one; the frequency and free-field energy laws are the push-forwards of the transverse momentum density under k -> c*|k| and k -> hbar*c*|k|, with means whenever the first moment is finite; and the one-photon momentum-component readouts are the push-forwards under k -> hbar*k_j, with means whenever the corresponding absolute first moment is finite. The frequency, energy and momentum-component variances are finite and strictly positive on their multiplier domains. The result is conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model, records no detector, no sampling model and no measured number, and shows that no normalisable one-photon vector has sharp frequency, energy or momentum.

items.title: The declared ideal counting, energy-window and analyser detection models of the radiation sector
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement
postulate P3 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], in
the measurement vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]].
Assume Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]),
including the hypotheses inherited from the radiation postulate and the cited
measurement mathematics.

**(b) Declared ideal total-number detector.** The **declared ideal
total-number detector** of the radiation sector is the declared ideal sharp
measurement with outcome set $\mathbb N$, outcome projection
$$P_{n}:=\Pi_{n}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
the sector projections of the Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$; the family
$(\Pi_{n})$ consists of mutually orthogonal orthogonal projections with strong
sum $I$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]] clauses
(a),(b),(c)). Its **count law** in a declared radiation preparation $\rho$ is
the reading of clause (ii) of P2,
$$p_{n}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_{n}),\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}p_{n}(\rho)=1,$$
and its **number readout** is the assigned total-number observable $(N,1)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] read through the atom
law of P2. The conditional post-count state and the discarded-outcome state are
the Lueders updates of the measurement definition
([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]],
[[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]). The word "count" refers to
the quanta of the declared model; no laboratory counter, no absorption
process, no detection efficiency, no dark count, no dead time and no
background is declared here.

**(c) Declared ideal energy-window detector.** For a Borel set
$B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ read in joules the **declared ideal energy-window
detector of window $B$** is the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome
structure
$$\bigl(E_{H_f}(B),\ I-E_{H_f}(B)\bigr),$$
where $E_{H_f}$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of the assigned
free-field energy observable $(H_f,\mathrm J)$; its **window law** in the
preparation $\rho$ is $p_{B}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_f}(B))$ and its
complement probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I-E_{H_f}(B)))$, the reading
of P2. A finite-resolution detector is described by such a window or by a
declared finite or countably infinite family $(B_a)_{a\in A}$ of pairwise
disjoint Borel windows covering $[0,\infty)$, with outcome projections
$(E_{H_f}(B_a))_{a\in A}$. Countable additivity of the spectral PVM and
$E_{H_f}([0,\infty))=I$ give their strong sum $I$, so this is an admissible
declared ideal sharp measurement. The
statement that a laboratory spectrometer realizes a declared window, with what
resolution and calibration, is an identification under P7.

**(d) Declared analyser detection.** The **declared polarisation-analyser
detection** of the fixed propagation mode is the analyser family
$\{P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\}$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], read as a
declared ideal sharp measurement of the polarisation factor; its law and its conditional update are proved on this page. It detects the polarisation alternative of the model and is not a photon counter.

**(e) Repetition requires a separate sampling model.** The declaration of a
detector gives the outcome law of a single declared measurement. A prediction
for repeated trials, a count rate, or any statistical comparison with data
requires in addition a declared preparation-and-apparatus model and a sampling
model in the sense of P7 -- for instance an identically-and-independently
repeated preparation with a declared number of trials -- which this page does
not supply. A single measurement outcome law is not a frequency and no
frequency is asserted.

**(f) Destructive detectors are outside the declared class.** A
photoabsorption detector that destroys the absorbed quantum, and any detector
whose post-outcome state of the radiation field is not the Lueders update,
requires its own declared instrument, that is its own outcome effects together
with its own conditional updates (clause (v) of P3, clause (d) of the
measurement definition). No such instrument is declared on this page, and the
"blocked" outcome of the analyser is used only through its discarded-outcome
law.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (b)-(d) fix vocabulary and read the cited postulates;
they add no physical assumption beyond P1-P3, P7 and the radiation model, and
they assert no detection mechanism, no response function and no empirical
result. In particular, the declaration of an ideal counting model is not a
claim that any physical device counts photons, and the energy-window model is
not a claim that any physical spectrometer measures exact energy.
items.physical_scope: The declared ideal detection models of the radiation sector: the ideal total-number counting model with the Fock sector projections as outcome structure and the Born law of P2, the ideal energy-window model with the spectral projections of the free-field energy, and the polarisation analyser of the fixed-mode model. The declaration fixes vocabulary only; it asserts no laboratory counter, no absorption instrument, no efficiency, no dark counts, no dead time, no background, no calibration and no sampling model, and repeated trials require a separately declared statistical model.

items.title: Number and energy statistics of a declared mode: number states, coherent states and the continuum thermal limitation
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]),
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, a
dimensionless label $z\in\mathbb C$, and write $U:=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. Then:

(a) for every $n\in\mathbb N$ the $n$-quanta mode vector $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$
is a unit vector of the $n$-photon sector; the count law of the declared ideal
total-number detector in the preparation of its ray is
$p_{m}=\delta_{mn}$, and the number readout is $n$ with probability one;

(b) the count law of the mode-coherent preparation $U\psi_{z}$ of label $z$ is
the Poisson law
$$p_{n}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
with mean and variance
$$\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,p_{n}=|z|^{2},\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^{2}p_{n}-\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,p_{n}\Bigr)^{2}=|z|^{2};$$
in particular the mode-coherent preparation is not a number state unless
$z=0$;

(c) if $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, with unit-mode coordinates
$\varphi(k)$ in $\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$ as in clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], and writing
$\bar\varepsilon:=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\hbar c\int|k|\,\|\varphi(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$,
the energy means of the assigned free-field energy observable are
$$\langle H_f\rangle_{Ue_{n}}=n\,\bar\varepsilon,\qquad \langle H_f\rangle_{U\psi_{z}}=|z|^{2}\,\bar\varepsilon ;$$

(d) under the same condition $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing
$\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}:=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^2$,
the energy variances are
$$\operatorname{Var}_{Ue_{n}}(H_f)=n\bigl(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_{U\psi_{z}}(H_f)=|z|^{2}\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}} ;$$
the first is strictly positive for every $n\ge1$ and the second is strictly
positive for every $z\ne0$. Thus $Ue_n$ has non-sharp energy for $n\ge1$
and $U\psi_z$ has non-sharp energy for $z\ne0$. At $n=0$ or $z=0$ the
corresponding preparation is the vacuum $\Omega$, with $H_f\Omega=0$ and
energy law $\delta_0$;

(e) *full-sector Gibbs limitation*: let $\beta>0$ have SI unit
$\mathrm J^{-1}$, so that $\beta H_f$ is dimensionless. The bounded operator
$e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not compact and hence not trace class; therefore it does
not define a density operator by trace normalization on the full transverse
continuum sector. This conclusion rules out only that trace-normalized
full-sector Gibbs form. Other mode-selected, regularized or otherwise
separately defined preparations are outside this theorem; no identification of
$\beta$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature and no thermal interpretation
of any state is asserted here;

(f) all assertions are conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model
and use only the declared ideal counting model. No measured count, frequency,
efficiency or temperature is asserted, and no sampling model is introduced.
items.physical_scope: The conditional number and energy statistics of a declared normalisable mode of the adopted radiation sector: the n-quanta mode state has sharp count n; the mode-coherent state has the Poisson count law of dimensionless parameter |z|^2 with mean and variance |z|^2; the energy means and variances of these preparations are computed from the mode profile, are strictly positive in variance for n>=1 and z!=0 (the vacuum cases have zero variance), and the full-sector Gibbs operator e^(-beta H_f) is not trace class for beta>0 in J^-1. This excludes only its trace-normalized Gibbs density form; other preparations are outside the theorem. The result is conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model, uses the ideal counting model only, reports no measured count and asserts no thermalisation or temperature identification.

Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 5.3 printed pages 48-50 and Section 4 printed pages 26-41: number states with energy increment hbar*omega, coherent states with mean photon number |alpha|^2, and the Poisson number distribution of a coherent state

S. Pratt, Lecture Notes on Quantum Mechanics (Michigan State University, PHY 851/852; retrieved via the Internet Archive snapshot of 2024-04-21), Chapter 14 Section 14.2 printed pages 220-222: coherent states as preparations without definite particle number, their normalization and their number expectation and variance

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the photons and radiation modes page
items.statement:
**What the page adopts.** The page adopts the radiation extension of the
framework, [[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]:
a fixed propagation-mode one-photon polarisation model with a two-dimensional
transverse internal space, a quantised free transverse radiation sector with
bosonic Fock space, and the mode assignments $\omega=c|k|$,
$E=\hbar\omega$ and $p=\hbar k$ in a declared inertial chart. These are
additional model assumptions of the framework; they are not derived from P1-P7,
not derived from classical Maxwell theory or special relativity, and not
obtained as a limit of the massive one-particle model. The page also adopts the
preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]])
for every reading of a detector outcome.

**What the page proves conditionally.**
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] fix the
model vocabulary, units and domains.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] proves the Born
outcome law $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$, $\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ of the
declared ideal analyser, its affinity over mixtures, its phase invariance and
the conditional update of a repeated ideal analyser.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-one-photon-number-energy-and-momentum-laws]] proves that a
normalisable one-photon preparation has the sharp number readout one, the
frequency and energy laws given by the push-forwards of $\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$
under $c|k|$ and $\hbar c|k|$ (a unit packet coordinate $f(k)$ has units
$\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$), their means under the first-moment condition, and
the corresponding momentum-component laws and means under absolute
first-moment integrability. Frequency, energy and momentum variances are
strictly positive and finite on the corresponding multiplier domains; the
singleton probabilities vanish for every normalisable unit vector without a
moment-domain hypothesis.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] proves the sharp
count of the $n$-quanta mode state, the Poisson count law and moments of the
mode-coherent preparation, the energy means and variances of those
preparations, and that $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not trace class for the full
continuum sector when $\beta>0$ has unit $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Thus its
trace-normalized full-sector Gibbs density is unavailable; other preparations
are outside the theorem. All these are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and
the adopted radiation model in the declared measurement models. The repeated
ideal-analyser conditional update additionally adopts P3
([[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]); its use is restricted
to outcomes of positive probability. Their units are recorded in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] and in the assigned observables
of the model.

**What the page does not claim.** The page does not derive the radiation
extension from Maxwell's equations, does not derive a Lorentz transformation
law for mode labels, polarisations or energies, and does not assert Galilean
covariance of the radiation sector; the two polarisation states of the photon
are adopted, and their relativistic description by Lorentz-group
representations is outside this non-relativistic extension. It does not
introduce a photon position wave function, a photon localisation operator or a
general photon-position distribution; the sharp-mode label $k$ is a spectral
parameter and not a state, and no normalisable one-photon vector has sharp
frequency, energy or momentum. It does not supply a light-matter Hamiltonian, a
dipole coupling, selection rules, absorption or stimulated emission, and it
does not supply vacuum spontaneous emission; those belong to the later pair
on light-matter and spectral transitions, where the coupling and environment
assumptions are declared separately.

**What the page's idealisations are.** The declared analyser, the declared
total-number detector and the declared energy-window detector are ideal
projection-valued measurements of the model
([[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]). No
laboratory polariser, counter or spectrometer is identified with them; no
efficiency, dark count, dead time, background, calibration or resolution is
declared, and a destructive absorption detector would require its own
instrument. A single measurement law is not a frequency: repeated trials
require a separately declared preparation and sampling model in the sense of
P7, which this page does not supply.

**Empirical status.** The page records no experiment, no measured count, no
calibration, no uncertainty budget and no statistical test, and none is
invented. The Born ratio $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ of the declared analyser
coincides with the intensity ratio of the declared classical transverse-field
model of the companion page; the coincidence is a property of the two declared
models and does not establish field quantisation, and classical
electromagnetic waves also interfere. Whether a given source, polariser or
detector is described by the declared fixed-mode model is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7; agreement of the model's conditional
predictions with reported data would be evidence about the combined model and
apparatus assumptions, not a deductive proof of the model or of the framework.

**Mathematical hypotheses.** The conditional deductions summarized here retain the choice hypotheses of their mathematical suppliers; in particular, the transverse free-field Fock supplier assumes Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice. [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]] record these assumptions.

items.title: Malus and Jones ratios of the declared analyser: the same cos^2 from the Born law and from a classical transverse amplitude
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] with polarisation
space $V$, orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$ and analyser projections
$P_{\theta}$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an angle
$\theta\in\mathbb R$. This example compares two declared models of the same
analyser:

**(a) The quantised-model ratio.** Consider the pure one-photon polarisation
preparation of the ray $[e_{1}]$ and the declared ideal analyser at angle
$\theta$. By
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] the outcome law of
the analyser is
$$p_{+1}=\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta,\qquad p_{-1}=\sin^{2}\theta,$$
so the **transmitted Born probability** is $\cos^{2}\theta$ in the unit $1$ of
dimensionless probabilities.

**(b) The declared classical transverse-amplitude model.** Declare the
following elementary model, with no claim that it is Maxwell theory: its
**field data** are complex vectors $E\in V$ whose coordinates are dimensionless
amplitude ratios relative to one fixed reference amplitude $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$;
no absolute field strength is assigned. The **analyser at angle $\theta$**
acts on the field data by the orthogonal projection
$$E\longmapsto P_{\theta}E;$$
the model's **declared dimensionless relative intensity** of a field datum is
$$I(E):=\|E\|^{2},$$
and the **transmitted intensity fraction** is $I(P_{\theta}E)/I(E)$ for
$E\ne0$.
This is a declared idealisation of the classical description of a
polariser as projecting the transverse field amplitude (the Jones-vector
reading); it imports no Maxwell equation and makes no detector claim.

The example computes both ratios for the same declared data and compares them.
items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional model comparison on the declared fixed propagation-mode polarisation space: the Born probability cos^2(theta) of the quantised model's ideal analyser for the preparation along e_1, and the dimensionless relative-intensity ratio cos^2(theta) of a declared normalized classical transverse complex amplitude passed through the same projection. The example establishes that the two declared models agree on this ratio and asserts no field quantisation, no detector claim, no Maxwell derivation and no empirical result.

items.title: Number statistics of a single declared mode: sharp, Poisson and geometric preparations
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]),
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$ with
coordinate representatives in $\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$ by clause (b)
of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]];
write $U=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] and let the dimensionless label
$z\in\mathbb C$ and a
**declared effective mode energy** $E_{0}>0$ in joules (equivalently a
declared effective frequency $\omega_{0}=E_{0}/\hbar>0$ in
$\mathrm s^{-1}$) be given parameters of this example. The example compares the
count statistics of the following three **declared preparations** of the mode
subspace, all read with the declared ideal total-number detector:

**(a) The $n$-quanta mode state.** For $n\in\mathbb N$, the pure preparation of
the ray of $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$.

**(b) The mode-coherent state.** The pure preparation of the ray of
$U\psi_{z}$, with dimensionless coherent-state label $z$ and
$\psi_{z}=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{m}\frac{z^{m}}{\sqrt{m!}}e_{m}$.

**(c) The declared effective-energy mode preparation.** For a parameter
$\beta>0$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$, the density operator
$$\rho_{\beta,E_{0}}:=(1-q)\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}q^{n}\,T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}},\qquad q:=e^{-\beta E_{0}}\in(0,1),$$
the transfer to the mode subspace of the single-mode weights of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] with its parameter
$\omega$ set equal to the declared effective energy $E_{0}$. This is
a declared conditional preparation of the model, not a derivation from any
radiation-matter interaction and not a statement that the mode is in thermal
equilibrium.

The example computes the count law, mean and variance of the three
preparations. It compares (b) and (c) at equal positive mean, and includes
(a) in that comparison when the common mean is a positive integer and $n$
is chosen equal to it.
items.physical_scope: A conditional computation of the count statistics of three declared preparations of one normalisable mode: the sharp count of an n-quanta mode state, the Poisson count law of the mode-coherent preparation, and the geometric count law of a declared effective-mode-energy Gibbs-type preparation. The example is conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model, declares its mode-energy parameter explicitly, records no measurement, no sampling model and no temperature identification, and asserts no thermalisation.

items.title: A two-bin comparison of a declared classical field model and the quantised model: identical normalised laws do not discriminate
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension
postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] with polarisation
space $V$ and orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$. Assume the Axioms of Countable
Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Declare the following **two-bin comparison**:

1. an orthonormal pair $(u_{+},u_{-})$ of $V$, read as the pair of orthogonal
   **fringe bin directions** of a declared two-bin detector, with projections
   $Q_{\pm}x:=\langle x,u_{\pm}\rangle u_{\pm}$;
2. a **declared amplitude datum** $a\in V\setminus\{0\}$ whose complex
   coordinates are dimensionless ratios relative to one fixed reference
   amplitude $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$; $a$ need not have unit norm;
3. the **declared classical field model**, whose state datum is the
   amplitude coordinate $a$ relative to $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$, whose dimensionless relative bin intensities are
   $I_{\pm}(a):=\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}$, and whose
   normalised two-bin law is $I_{\pm}(a)/(I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a))$;
4. the **quantised model reading** of the same datum: the pure preparation of
   the ray $[a]$ of the polarisation space, measured by the declared ideal
   sharp measurement with outcome projections $(Q_{+},Q_{-})$ declared directly in the sense of
   [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
   clause (a), with the Born law of P2. This arbitrary-bin sharp measurement
   need not belong to the real-angle analyser family of the original frame.

Then:

(a) $Q_{+}+Q_{-}=I$ and the normalised stated laws of the two declared models
coincide for every datum $a\ne0$:
$$\frac{I_{\pm}(a)}{I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a)}=p_{\pm}([a])=\frac{\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}}{\|a\|^{2}}=\frac{|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}}{\|a\|^{2}};$$

(b) writing $a=a_{1}+a_{2}$ for any declared decomposition of the datum into
two **path components**, both declared laws contain the interference
cross-term
$$\frac{2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\langle u_{\pm},a_{1}\rangle\,\overline{\langle u_{\pm},a_{2}\rangle}\bigr)}{\|a\|^{2}},$$
so the presence of a fringe pattern of this two-bin form does not distinguish
the two declared models;

(c) the two declared models are nevertheless different physical models: in the
classical model the datum is a field amplitude with a deterministic intensity,
while in the quantised model it is a state ray with a Born law; a discriminator
requires a prediction on which two fully specified models differ, together
with a declared detector response, preparation and sampling model in the
sense of P7. Count statistics on a declared number-state preparation are a
candidate for a further comparison only after a classical field-and-detector
count law and the corresponding preparations in both models are declared.
The deterministic classical intensities do not supply that count law, so no
count-statistics discriminator follows from the present declarations;

(d) this item constructs no such discriminating comparison and reports no
data; it asserts no measurement, no count, no frequency and no empirical
conclusion, and it does not claim that the classical model agrees with the
quantised model beyond the declared two-bin law.

The result is that the normalised laws coincide for every declared amplitude, so such a pattern does not discriminate the two declared models; the thought experiment records the cross-term (interference) structure common to both and asserts no experiment, no counts, no detector response and no empirical conclusion.
